meta.title: Pragma Chess — an open source chess database for studying, training and playing
meta.description: Pragma Chess keeps your games in databases and lets you study them with an engine, an opening book and your notes; train against the engine with a tutor; play online. Light, simple, with what really matters. Windows, macOS, Linux.

hero.title: Your chess, in one place.
hero.lead: An open source chess database for studying, training and playing: light, simple, with what really matters.
hero.note: Free, MIT licensed. For Windows, macOS and Linux.

features.title: What it does
features.lead: Everything a chess player needs to keep, study and improve — and nothing in the way.

items.title: Databases of games
items.text: Your games in .pdb databases: import PGN, lichess.org and chess.com games, torneionline.com tournaments and ChessBase files. Search by position, variation, player, opening, tournament and year.

items.title: Explain
items.text: Press E and the engine shows on the board why the last move is good or bad: red arrows where material falls, blue arrows for the reply that makes the difference, a forced mate played out.

items.title: Variations and notes
items.text: Play a move that is not the next one and it becomes a variation, shown under the move it replaces. Annotate moves with !, ?, ±, ∞… Everything is saved with the game and travels in PGN.

items.title: Training with a tutor
items.text: Play against the engine, from the opening book you tune. When your move is a mistake the tutor stops the game and lets you take it back, explain it or go on.

items.title: Play online
items.text: Connect your lichess.org account, or freechess.org even as a guest, and play people from the same board. While you play, the engine, Explain and the book are off: it is you against your opponent.

items.title: Opening books
items.text: Polyglot books with your repertoire and the weights you choose, so the engine trains you on the lines you want. Named openings in English and Italian.

items.title: Sync between computers
items.text: Keep your databases and projects the same on every computer through an FTP, WebDAV or Git folder, and on your phone with the companion app. Nothing is ever deleted without a merge.

items.title: Projects
items.text: Database, game, move, panels and engine are a project you reopen as you left it. Native desktop interface, in English and Italian.

formats.name: .pdb databases
formats.text: SQLite files you can copy, share and open with other tools; one database per collection of games.

formats.name: .pch projects
formats.text: readable YAML with the database, the game, the engine and the arrangement of the panels.

formats.name: PGN and Polyglot
formats.text: the standard formats for games and opening books, in and out.

support.title: Support and community
support.lead: Pragma Chess is made in the open, with chess clubs and players.

items.title: Guide
items.text: The guide is built into the application (Help ▸ Pragma Chess Guide, F1), with a search field, in English and Italian.

items.title: Report a problem
items.text: Something wrong, or missing? Open an issue on GitHub with what you did and what you saw.

items.title: Questions and ideas
items.text: Ask how to do something, propose what is missing, show what you made with it: the project's Discussions on GitHub.

items.title: Contribute
items.text: The code is MIT licensed: C++ and Qt, the desktop client and its database engine alike. Pull requests are welcome.

footer.license: Pragma Chess is free software under the MIT License.
footer.credits: Built with Qt. Default engine: Stockfish (GPL v3). Opening names from lichess-org/chess-openings (CC0). Pieces: Good Companion.
